findings.evidence: Lines 207-232 state the general theorems with `hrow`/`hcol`; lines 240-265 re-derive the same content for `V = 1` from `*_def`. `Matrix.one_apply` gives `‖1 i j‖ ^ 2 = if i = j then 1 else 0`, whose row and column sums over a `Fintype` are `1`, discharging `hrow` and `hcol`.
findings.fix: Prove once `(i : n) → ∑ j, ‖(1 : Matrix n n ℂ) i j‖ ^ 2 = 1` and its column twin (`Matrix.one_apply`, Mathlib/Data/Matrix/Diagonal.lean:234), then derive all four `_one` lemmas from `f2CCMinus_eq_of_sum_norm_sq_eq_one` and siblings plus `Finset.sum_add_distrib`/`Finset.sum_sub_distrib`.
findings.issue: `f2CCMinus_one`, `xf3CCMinus_one` (248), `f2CCPlus_one` (255), `xf3CCPlus_one` (262) are each proved from scratch (`simp [*_def, Matrix.one_apply, apply_ite ...]`), but they are exactly the `V = 1` instances of the general `*_eq_of_sum_norm_sq_eq_one` theorems proved just above: `∑ᵢ (a i + b i) = ∑ᵢ a i + ∑ᵢ b i`, so e.g. `2x Σᵢ(u_i + d̄_i)` is literally `2x(Σᵢ u_i + Σᵢ d̄_i)`. The same `Matrix.one_apply`/`apply_ite` computation is duplicated four times instead of once.

findings.evidence: Lines 317-320: `hquark` applies `hq _` only at `up i`, `hantiquark` applies `hqbar _` only at `down j`; no other use of `hq`/`hqbar` appears in the proof.
findings.fix: Weaken to the active channels: `(hq : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f (quark (up i)) x Q2) (hqbar : ∀ j, 0 ≤ f (antiquark (down j)) x Q2)` for the `W⁻` lemmas, and the `down`-quark/`up`-antiquark pair for the `W⁺` ones; the existing proofs go through unchanged (`hq _`/`hqbar _` at lines 318, 320), and callers holding `IsPartonDensity.nonneg` can still supply them.
findings.issue: `abs_xf3CCMinus_le_f2CCMinus` assumes `hq : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (quark a) x Q2` and `hqbar : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f (antiquark a) x Q2` over the whole flavour type, but the proof uses only `hq (up i)` and `hqbar (down j)`. Same in `abs_xf3CCPlus_le_f2CCPlus` (325), `f2CCMinus_nonneg` (332), `f2CCPlus_nonneg` (337). This is stronger than needed exactly in the rectangular/active-subset setting the module advertises, where `up`/`down` cover only part of `Flavor`.

summary: The definitions sit at the right level (arbitrary index types, rectangular mixing matrix, row/column unit-norm as explicit hypotheses rather than a unitary type). Two generality defects: the four `V = 1` lemmas re-prove from the definition a case that is a direct instance of the general unit-norm theorems, and the four positivity lemmas assume non-negativity over the whole flavour type when only the active channels are used.
